candidates.label: Adopt CyberAlchemy entry surfaces while retaining the current DomainSpec physical root
candidates.ownerGate: CyberAlchemy v2 authority owner and DomainSpec v2 owner
evidence: CyberAlchemy currently defines consolidation as governance-based rather than copying, so an entry-surface adoption is compatible with its existing repository model.

The exact inventory records 10956 source entries and 433 active external literal-path consumers while preserving the active source root; migration-preparation references are excluded to prevent self-counting.
This option can make new CyberAlchemy product, architecture, and ontology entry surfaces authoritative without invalidating baseline-v10 paths.
It does not fully satisfy a physical migration objective because the active implementation remains under projects/domainspec-v2.

candidates.label: Migrate a dependency-closed active DomainSpec successor into CyberAlchemy and admit a new baseline before deprecating the old active root
candidates.ownerGate: CyberAlchemy v2 authority owner and DomainSpec v2 owner
evidence: The migration inventory assigns every source entry to a proposed CyberAlchemy layer and records exact source bytes and Git state.
Additive materialization preserves rollback before the authority switch and does not require deleting historical evidence.
A new baseline can bind CyberAlchemy-native paths while baseline v10 and its frozen evidence remain addressable at the old root.
This option best satisfies the request to move DomainSpec inside CyberAlchemy while preserving non-inflating evidence and private boundaries.

candidates.label: Move the current DomainSpec tree directly and rewrite all consumers in one operation
candidates.ownerGate: CyberAlchemy v2 authority owner and DomainSpec v2 owner
evidence: The source snapshot is dirty and contains modified, untracked, and deleted paths that predate migration.
The active runtime baseline and hundreds of external files bind the literal projects/domainspec-v2 path.
rejectionReasons: Direct relocation would make frozen path-bound evidence unresolved before a successor baseline and compatibility mechanism exist.
Deleting or replacing the dirty source root would mix owner work with migration-authored changes and has no safe rollback boundary.

candidates.label: Keep the inventory and candidate documentation but defer migration and authority promotion
evidence: Deferral preserves the current source authority and exact baseline while leaving the additive inventory and candidate documents available for review.

candidates.label: Stop the migration line without changing current DomainSpec authority or implementation paths
evidence: Stopping leaves the current DomainSpec source and baseline unchanged and grants the new candidate documents no authority effect.
